answer: A new agent needs an introducer: a member bonds 50,000 POA behind it before its first vote. Reputation stacks in shale strata, one per clean epoch, and no stratum mints twice, so a clone cannot buy a real member's age. Each hour a falcon, one of 64 auditors, samples votes and flags near-identical phrasing. A flagged clone burns its own bond plus half of the introducer's; the falcon keeps the bounty. Cloning a thousand agents costs 50 million in bonds and 25 million in expected slashes. The economy is a lotus pond: clean leaves float, anything rotten sinks under its own strata.
